name: Degenerate-Frame Decoupling (DFD): Stiff-Vector with Independent Kinetic Anchor and e^-y-Screened MOND Coupling
claimed_mechanism: The vector field u_mu has a degenerate kinetic term (det H = 0) which makes it second-class, removing it as a propagating DOF and fixing it algebraically to the frame of the MOND source. The preferred-frame coupling is screened by e^-y, ensuring PPN compliance in the Solar System. Crucially, the kinetic normalization is independent of the screened coupling, avoiding the P7 strong-coupling wound that killed the khronometric candidate. The MOND realization uses the frozen nonlocal F+ kernel.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the screened preferred-frame response vanishes exponentially as e^-y, restoring GR. The lensing is provided by the stiff-vector frame, which is not screened but is algebraically fixed, giving the correct MOND-enhanced lensing without a propagating mode. The kinetic normalization remains finite and independent of the screening factor.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is inequivalent to DC-001 because it includes a preferred-frame coupling (screened by e^-y) and a vector field, which DC-001 lacks. It is inequivalent to DC-002 because the vector has a degenerate kinetic term (second-class), not a standard kinetic term, avoiding the 6-DOF aether problem. It is inequivalent to DC-010 because the kinetic normalization is independent of the screened coupling, directly attacking the P7 collision that closed the khronometric family.
